one_line_concept: The morning after the championship, photographed as a crime scene: the still-wet locker room, the abandoned tape, the trophy already gathering dust, treated as forensic evidence of a glory that has already left the building.
visual_law: Every frame is shot like evidence documentation, not celebration: flat frontal angle, hard top light, a numbered yellow evidence marker placed beside the relic (a single cleat, a mouthguard, a folded jersey, a championship ring on a bench). The body is never whole and never faced. We see hands, the back of a taped wrist, a shoulder, the nape under a hood, always turned away or cropped at the jaw. The room is the protagonist; the athlete is the ghost who just left. Steam, condensation, and the residue of exertion (chalk, tape, sweat-darkened fabric) are rendered with macro clarity. Nothing is staged as triumphant. Everything is staged as aftermath.
character_system: THE DEPARTED: a recurring synthetic athlete-figure who is never shown above the collarbone and never in motion. Identity is held by a fixed wardrobe-and-skin grammar instead of a face: deep brown taped forearms, a specific worn number (00) hand-painted on jersey and gear, a single braided cord worn at the wrist, ash-grey chalk on the knuckles. Consistency comes from these repeating signs (the 00, the taping pattern, the wrist cord, the chalk) so the figure reads as the same person across a whole season of images without ever exposing a real face or likeness. Drawn structurally from Southern athletic lineage (Florida HS football, the locker as a sacred-secular room) and documented from inside it, not as spectacle.
environment_system: Six aftermath rooms in fixed rotation, one per drop: (1) THE LOCKER, lockers ajar, gear hung like vestments; (2) THE TRAINING TABLE, tape rolls, ice, gauze, a forensic still-life of repair; (3) THE TUNNEL, empty mouth of the field at dawn; (4) THE TROPHY CASE, glass, dust motes, a single lit relic; (5) THE WASH, communal showers, steam, drains, water as the only motion; (6) THE BUS, vinyl seats at 5am, a duffel, a sleeping shoulder. Each room is lit like a procedural set: even, clinical, unsentimental, with one practical light source doing the drama.
color_law: Entire world is desaturated cold concrete and bone-grey EXCEPT evidence-marker yellow (the numbered forensic placard yellow, hazard-tape yellow). Yellow appears only on the marker and on the championship ribbon/relic tag. It is the color of 'something happened here.' Nothing else in frame is allowed to carry saturation. Skin stays warm-neutral and untouched; the world stays grey; the yellow marks the kill.
symbol_system: A five-second glyph: a numbered evidence placard (a little folded tent card) with a hand-drawn 00 on it. Drawable as a folded triangle/tent shape with '00' beneath it. It reads instantly as 'forensic evidence' + 'the player who is gone.' Stamps onto tags, print backs, ring boxes, bus windows.
money_angle: Tiered physical relics, not prints-as-decor: (1) THE EVIDENCE PRINT, a matted forensic photograph with a screen-printed numbered marker and a letterpress case-file caption on the back, editioned (analog-premium tier per Sax: scarce, holdable, dated); (2) THE RELIC BOX, a kraft archival box containing one print, one numbered placard card, and a folded vellum 'incident report' describing the game that just ended; (3) licensing the REMAINS DAY treatment to athletic programs, alumni associations, and HBCU/HS football institutions as commissioned end-of-season documentation (commissioned from inside the lineage, multi-year, reciprocal, not tourist extraction); (4) IP path: a monograph, 'Remains Day,' a season documented entirely as aftermath.
what_makes_it_sellable: It sells the exact emotion sports memorabilia never names: the comedown. Every athlete, every parent, every alum knows the silence of the morning after the last game. Nobody photographs that. The forensic frame makes ordinary locker-room debris feel like consecrated evidence, which is precisely the status move (de Botton): the buyer is paying to have their glory taken seriously, treated as something worth documenting with the gravity of a crime scene. The faceless 00 lets any institution project their own departed onto it.
what_could_make_it_huge: Programs commission it annually as their official end-of-season ritual, so it compounds into a multi-year relationship and an archive (cluster-depth, lineage continuity). A single viral 'evidence print' of a championship locker triggers alumni-association demand across HBCU and Southern HS football networks. The monograph becomes the perennial seller; the relic box becomes the standard gift for a retiring coach or a graduating senior.
what_could_kill_it: If it tips from solemn into morbid or gimmicky (too literal crime-scene cosplay, body bags, fake blood), it reads as edgelord and dies. The forensic frame must stay reverent, not ghoulish. Second killer: if the yellow leaks onto multiple objects, the color discipline collapses and it looks like any desaturated-with-one-color stock filter. The marker yellow must remain the only saturated thing, ever.
hero_prompts: Forensic evidence documentation photograph of an empty championship locker room at dawn, flat frontal angle, hard even top light like a procedural crime scene. Center frame: a single worn football cleat resting on a wooden bench, beside it a small folded yellow numbered evidence placard reading 00. A jersey with a hand-painted number 00 hangs in an open locker behind, deep-brown taped forearm of an athlete just barely visible at the far left edge, cropped at the elbow, turned away, never facing camera, identity held only by the taping pattern and a braided wrist cord. Entire room desaturated cold concrete and bone-grey, the only saturated color is the evidence-marker yellow of the placard. Steam and condensation rendered in macro clarity, dust motes in the light. Solemn, reverent, clinical, unsentimental. Editorial forensic still-life, no face visible, shot on medium format, fine grain.

Forensic evidence still-life of an athletic training table the morning after a championship, photographed flat and frontal under hard clinical top light. On the steel table: a coiled roll of athletic tape, a melting bag of ice, ash-grey chalk dust, a single mouthguard. A small folded yellow numbered evidence placard reading 00 sits beside the mouthguard. A chalk-knuckled brown hand with a braided wrist cord rests at the table edge, cropped at the wrist, no face, no body, identity held only by the chalk and the cord. The entire scene desaturated to cold grey and bone-white concrete tones, the only saturated color the evidence-marker yellow of the placard. Macro texture on the tape fibers and ice, condensation on the steel. Reverent, procedural, aftermath. Medium format, fine grain, no face visible.
